Toxicology Chapter 180

Antipsychotics

Antipsychotic toxicity is usually supportive-care heavy, but exam questions focus on CNS depression, orthostatic hypotension, QT/QRS effects, acute dystonia/akathisia, and neuroleptic malignant syndrome.

Board lens: NMS = fever + lead-pipe rigidity + altered mental status + autonomic instability after dopamine antagonist exposure. Differentiate from serotonin syndrome by bradyreflexia/rigidity/slower onset rather than clonus/hyperreflexia.

Overview

Tintinalli Source Check
Tintinalli Source Check
D2 blockadeExtrapyramidal symptoms, hyperprolactinemia, NMS risk.
Alpha-1 blockadeOrthostatic hypotension and reflex tachycardia.
Muscarinic blockadeDry mucosa, mydriasis, urinary retention, tachycardia, hyperthermia.
Histamine blockadeSedation and CNS depression.

Clinical Features of Overdose

Tintinalli Source Check
Common pattern: CNS depression, paradoxical agitation/delirium, seizures in some agents, sinus tachycardia, orthostatic hypotension, QT prolongation, and anticholinergic findings.

ECG and Overdose Treatment

Tintinalli Source Check
FindingTreatmentHigh-yield note
SeizureBenzodiazepinesLorazepam commonly used.
HypotensionIV fluids; norepinephrine/phenylephrine if neededAvoid dopamine in antipsychotic overdose.
QTc >500 ms / torsades riskMagnesium sulfate 2 g IVCorrect Mg/K.
QRS widening / ventricular dysrhythmiaSodium bicarbonateAvoid class Ia/Ic/III antiarrhythmics.

Extrapyramidal Symptoms

Tintinalli Source Check
Acute dystoniaFace/tongue/neck spasm, oculogyric crisis. Treat diphenhydramine or benztropine.
AkathisiaSubjective restlessness; may be mistaken for worsening psychosis.
Tardive dyskinesiaLate, often not readily reversible.

Drug Dose Reference

ProblemTreatment ReferenceBoard Caution
Acute dystoniaDiphenhydramine 25-50 mg IV or benztropine 1-2 mg IV; continue PO 2-3 daysSymptoms can recur because causative agent lasts longer.
AkathisiaReduce/stop offending agent; benztropine/diphenhydramine may help depending scenarioDo not misread as psychiatric agitation only.
QT prolongation/torsadesMagnesium sulfate 2 g IV; repeat/infuse if neededQTc >500 ms is high-risk.
QRS wideningSodium bicarbonate 1-2 mEq/kg IV bolus, repeat/infuse per responseAvoid procainamide, quinidine, amiodarone in conduction-toxic patients.
NMSStop antipsychotic; IV fluids/cooling; lorazepam 1-2 mg IV q2-4h as needed; consider dantrolene 1-2.5 mg/kg IV then 1 mg/kg q6h, bromocriptine 2.5 mg PO 3-4x/day, or amantadine 100 mg PO TIDDrug therapy is adjunctive; supportive care is the core.

Disposition

Tintinalli Source Check
Disposition: observe at least 6 hours; check orthostatics, ambulation, mental status, ECG. Admit for toxicity, ECG abnormality, persistent orthostatic hypotension, seizure, respiratory depression, acidosis, or severe symptoms.

Key Points

Overdose is usually supportiveAirway, monitoring, ECG, glucose, fluids.
QT/QRSQT >500: magnesium. QRS widening: sodium bicarbonate.
HypotensionFluids then norepinephrine/phenylephrine; avoid dopamine.
Acute dystoniaDiphenhydramine or benztropine, then oral continuation.
NMS tetradAMS, rigidity, fever, autonomic instability.
NMS vs serotoninNMS slower + bradyreflexia/lead-pipe; serotonin rapid + clonus/hyperreflexia.
NMS treatmentStop drug, cool, fluids, benzodiazepines, airway support; consider dantrolene/bromocriptine/amantadine.
DispositionNormal early exam is not enough if ECG/orthostatics/mental status abnormal.

Chapter Assessment

Most common cardiovascular manifestations of antipsychotic overdose?

Why each choice is right or wrong
A. Sinus tachycardia and orthostatic hypotension
Correct choice
Tintinalli emphasizes sinus tachycardia and orthostatic hypotension as common.
B. Profound bradycardia in all patients
Incorrect choice
Bradycardia is not the common pattern.
C. Hypertension with widened pulse pressure only
Incorrect choice
This is not typical.
D. Asystole without prodrome
Incorrect choice
Rare severe cases occur, but this is not the usual manifestation.

Antipsychotic overdose with QTc >500 ms should receive:

Why each choice is right or wrong
A. Magnesium sulfate
Correct choice
Magnesium sulfate is recommended for QTc prolongation/torsades risk.
B. Naloxone only
Incorrect choice
Naloxone may be considered for respiratory depression differential, not QT treatment.
C. Physostigmine
Incorrect choice
Physostigmine is not treatment for antipsychotic QT prolongation.
D. Sodium nitrite
Incorrect choice
Sodium nitrite is for cyanide antidote kits.

Treatment of QRS widening/ventricular dysrhythmia from antipsychotic toxicity includes:

Why each choice is right or wrong
A. Sodium bicarbonate
Correct choice
Sodium bicarbonate is recommended for QRS prolongation and ventricular dysrhythmias.
B. Beta-blocker monotherapy
Incorrect choice
Not appropriate and may worsen instability.
C. Flumazenil
Incorrect choice
Flumazenil treats benzodiazepine effects and is risky in mixed overdose.
D. Cyproheptadine
Incorrect choice
Cyproheptadine is for serotonin syndrome, not QRS widening.

Acute dystonia after antipsychotic dose increase is treated with:

Why each choice is right or wrong
A. Diphenhydramine or benztropine
Correct choice
Tintinalli lists diphenhydramine 25-50 mg IV or benztropine 1-2 mg IV.
B. High-dose acetaminophen
Incorrect choice
Antipyretic does not treat dystonia.
C. Calcium gluconate
Incorrect choice
Calcium is unrelated.
D. Hydroxocobalamin
Incorrect choice
Hydroxocobalamin treats cyanide toxicity.

Classic NMS clinical tetrad includes:

Why each choice is right or wrong
A. Altered mental status, muscle rigidity, fever, autonomic instability
Correct choice
This is the classic neuroleptic malignant syndrome pattern.
B. Miosis, bradypnea, hypothermia, constipation
Incorrect choice
This is opioid-like.
C. Clonus, diarrhea, diaphoresis, rapid onset within minutes
Incorrect choice
This better suggests serotonin syndrome.
D. Dry skin, urinary retention, normal reflexes, mydriasis only
Incorrect choice
This suggests anticholinergic toxicity.

Feature that favors serotonin syndrome over NMS?

Why each choice is right or wrong
A. Rapid onset with hyperreflexia/clonus
Correct choice
Serotonin syndrome tends to be rapid and has clonus/hyperreflexia.
B. Lead-pipe rigidity and bradyreflexia over days
Incorrect choice
This favors NMS.
C. Recent dopamine antagonist withdrawal
Incorrect choice
Dopamine antagonist withdrawal/exposure relates to NMS context.
D. Psychomotor slowing only
Incorrect choice
Nonspecific and not the best discriminator.

Core treatment of NMS includes:

Why each choice is right or wrong
A. Withdraw antipsychotic, IV fluids, external cooling, benzodiazepines, airway support as needed
Correct choice
Supportive care and withdrawal of offending drugs are central.
B. Continue antipsychotic to avoid relapse
Incorrect choice
Continuing offending agent worsens NMS.
C. Routine antipyretics only
Incorrect choice
Antipyretics do not treat muscle rigidity/hyperthermia mechanism.
D. Immediate discharge after one normal temperature
Incorrect choice
NMS needs admission/monitoring.

When an intubated NMS patient needs paralysis, preferred neuromuscular blocker type is:

Why each choice is right or wrong
A. Nondepolarizing agent such as rocuronium
Correct choice
Tintinalli prefers nondepolarizing agents when paralysis is required.
B. Succinylcholine
Incorrect choice
Depolarizing agents may worsen complications.
C. No paralytic ever
Incorrect choice
Severe rigidity/hyperthermia may need paralysis.
D. Physostigmine
Incorrect choice
Physostigmine is unrelated.

Disposition after antipsychotic ingestion with no toxicity requires at least:

Why each choice is right or wrong
A. Observation around 6 hours with orthostatics/ambulation and ECG assessment
Correct choice
Tintinalli describes at least 6 hours observation and discharge criteria if asymptomatic and no ECG/orthostatic issues.
B. Immediate discharge without ECG
Incorrect choice
Unsafe.
C. 48 hours ICU for every ingestion
Incorrect choice
Not necessary for all.
D. Dialysis before discharge
Incorrect choice
Dialysis is not routine.

Which antipsychotic adverse effect is typically early after starting/increasing dose and reversible?

Why each choice is right or wrong
A. Acute dystonia/akathisia
Correct choice
Acute dystonia and akathisia occur early and respond to anticholinergic therapy.
B. Tardive dyskinesia
Incorrect choice
Tardive dyskinesia is late and may be irreversible.
C. Drug-induced parkinsonism after prolonged use
Incorrect choice
Parkinsonism tends to develop later.
D. Agranulocytosis
Incorrect choice
Agranulocytosis is a hematologic adverse effect, not acute EPS.
